title: JavaScript Security Applied Check
description: Apply JavaScript security concepts by choosing safer DOM updates, validating input, handling auth storage, reasoning about CORS and CSRF, avoiding dynamic code risks, and protecting secrets.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: `preview.textContent = comment.body;`
`preview.innerHTML = comment.body;`
`eval(comment.body);`
`document.write(comment.body);`

questions.explanation: `textContent` displays the comment as text. The other options parse or run the value in unsafe ways.

questions.prompt: Which pattern is best when users may choose a sort field for an API request?

options.text: Allow only known fields such as `name`, `price`, or `createdAt`
Send any field name directly to the server without checks
Run the field name with `eval()` first
Store the field name as an access token

questions.explanation: An allow list keeps accepted values narrow and predictable.

options.text: Hiding a button improves UI but does not enforce server-side authorization
Buttons cannot be hidden with JavaScript
Only CSS can check roles
All users must see every button

questions.explanation: Frontend checks are useful for display, but the server must still enforce permissions for the action.

questions.prompt:
A form has this hidden input:
```html
<input type="hidden" name="price" value="1999">
```
What should the server do?

options.text: Calculate or verify the price from trusted server-side data
Trust the hidden input because users cannot see it
Treat hidden inputs as encrypted
Skip validation because the frontend supplied the value

questions.explanation: Hidden inputs are still user-controlled. Sensitive values like prices must be verified by the server.

questions.prompt: Which request is a better shape for changing profile data?

options.text: `fetch("/api/profile", { method: "PATCH", body: JSON.stringify(data) })` with server validation
`fetch("/api/delete-account")` using GET for a destructive action
A request that trusts only hidden form fields
A request that relies on CORS instead of authentication

questions.explanation: State-changing actions should use appropriate HTTP methods and must be validated by the server.

options.text: It may include cookies, so the server should be configured carefully and consider CSRF protections
It disables all cookies
It proves the response is public
It stores the user's password in localStorage

questions.explanation: `credentials: "include"` can send credentials on cross-origin requests when server policy allows it.

questions.prompt: A browser shows a CORS error when calling an admin API. What is the best security conclusion?

options.text: The server still needs authentication and authorization; CORS is not enough
The admin API is automatically secure
The route should allow every origin with credentials
The frontend should place an admin token in the URL

questions.explanation: CORS controls browser response reading. It does not replace server-side access control.

questions.prompt:
Which alternative is safer than this pattern?
```js
const calculate = new Function("price", `return ${formula}`);
```

options.text: Map allowed operation names to functions written by your code
Wrap the formula in `eval()`
Store the formula in a cookie
Disable HTTPS for the page

questions.explanation: Allowing users to choose from known operations keeps data separate from executable code.

options.text: It copies only expected properties and ignores unexpected keys
It deeply merges every property from input
It authenticates the user automatically
It makes all HTML safe to render with `innerHTML`

questions.explanation: Copying known properties makes the accepted data shape explicit and avoids blindly trusting unknown object keys.

questions.prompt: Which error handling pattern is safer for production users?

options.text: Log details for developers and show users a general helpful message
Show users the full stack trace and internal file paths
Put access tokens inside error messages
Ignore every error silently

questions.explanation: Users need useful messages, but internal details and sensitive data should not be exposed.

questions.prompt: A frontend app needs to call a payment provider using a private API key. What is the safest general approach?

options.text: Call your backend, and let the backend use the private key
Bundle the private key into frontend JavaScript
Put the private key in a comment
Send the key in the URL so it is easy to debug

questions.explanation: Private secrets must stay on the server. The frontend can call a backend endpoint that enforces validation and permissions.

questions.prompt: Which frontend behavior can support server-side rate limiting but not replace it?

options.text: Temporarily disabling a submit button while a request is in progress
Trusting every repeated request
Putting the rate limit value in a hidden input
Using `innerHTML` for all status messages

questions.explanation: Disabling a button improves user experience, but real rate limiting must be enforced by the server.

questions.prompt: Which code best builds a query string from user input?

options.text: `new URLSearchParams({ q: searchInput.value }).toString()`
`"q=" + searchInput.value` without encoding
`eval(searchInput.value)`
`document.write(searchInput.value)`

questions.explanation: `URLSearchParams` handles URL encoding for query parameter values.

questions.prompt: Which production error message is most appropriate after a failed save?

options.text: `We could not save your changes. Please try again.`
`Database password is ...`
`Stack trace: /srv/private/app/db.js:42`
`Authorization: Bearer ey...`

questions.explanation: A general helpful message avoids leaking sensitive internal details.

questions.prompt: Which checklist item is most important before rendering user-generated rich text?

options.text: Use a trusted sanitizer with a narrow allowed markup policy
Insert it directly with `innerHTML` because it came from a form
Store it in localStorage first to make it safe
Disable CORS

questions.explanation: If an app intentionally renders rich user HTML, it needs careful sanitization. Plain text should use text APIs.
